notes: Names printed without a suffix (BAYMILLER, CLEARWATER, AILANTHUS, BANK) are written with 'Street'. Freeman Avenue leans about 3 deg (centre ~1340 at Central, ~1285 at Clearwater, ~1215 at Bank); its west line is the sheet-225 block edge. Browne Alley (15') runs from Freeman east to the 28th District School lot, then the same 15 ft alley line continues east of the school lot to Baymiller (recorded as Browne Alley/Baymiller). Baymiller north of McMicken is 50 ft and includes public steps along its east side; south of the canal it is 40 ft. Clearwater (20') runs ESE from Freeman to Baymiller and continues east of Baymiller on the sheet-227 margin (20 ft opening at y~4767-4900), so Clearwater/Baymiller is a cross; near Baymiller a 2nd-floor pass bridges over it. Central/Baymiller: the two sides of Central are about 40 px out of line at Baymiller; the point is the mean of the two side centrelines. Unnamed 10 ft alleys ('?'): (1) N-S alley from Clearwater to Bank in the Freeman-Ailanthus block (x~2150 at the top, ~2123 at Bank); (2) E-W alley from Freeman to Ailanthus at y~6256, crossing (1); (3) N-S alley from Clearwater to Bank just west of the block-6 Baymiller lots (x~4259); (4) E-W alley from (3) east to Baymiller at y~6277. On '?'/'?' entries the first '?' is the N-S alley. Bank Street centre drifts from y~6975 at Freeman to ~7009 at Baymiller. A 4 in. water pipe runs east from Baymiller at y~6185 into sheet 227 but no street opening is drawn there on this sheet. Canal, tow path, foot bridge, scale bar and the block-2 rear yards are ignored. Browne Alley/Baymiller is marked cross because sheet 227 shows Browne Alley continuing east of Baymiller (this sheet's margin line east of Baymiller has no gap there). Wilmink Street (named on sheet 227) meets Baymiller from the east as a gap in the sheet-227 margin line (x~5082, gap from y~6368); its south side is hidden under the scale bar, so the Wilmink/Baymiller point is approximate (about +-25 px in y). It is ~150 px south of the unnamed alley entering from the west, so both are T.
